title: Split exterior comparison with lift independence and localization
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{p}W$ be $R$-linear maps such that $i$ is injective, $p$ is surjective and $\operatorname{im}i=\ker p$. Assume $W$ is projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. There exists an $R$-linear section $s:W\to V$ of $p$. For every such section, $t_s:U\oplus W\to V$, $t_s(u,w)=i(u)+s(w)$, is an isomorphism; its inverse sends $v$ to $(u,pv)$ where $i(u)=v-s(pv)$. These inverse maps and the section localize, and the localized sequence remains split exact at every multiplicative subset [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].
Assume in addition that $U,W$ are free modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with finite bases of lengths $r,s_0\geq0$. Use exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] and tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $c_{U,W}:\bigwedge^rU\otimes_R\bigwedge^{s_0}W\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigwedge^{r+s_0}(U\oplus W)$ be the canonical direct-sum comparison characterized by concatenating $(u_j,0)$ followed by $(0,w_k)$, and put $\theta_s=(\bigwedge^{r+s_0}t_s)\circ c_{U,W}$. This is an $R$-linear isomorphism. For arbitrary tuples $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in U$, $w_1,\ldots,w_{s_0}\in W$ and arbitrary lifts $v_k\in V$ with $p(v_k)=w_k$, it satisfies
$$\theta_s((u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_r)\otimes(w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_{s_0}))=i(u_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge i(u_r)\wedge v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{s_0}.$$
The map is independent of the section and of the chosen bases; the displayed formula holds for every replacement basis and every lift tuple. For a multiplicative subset $T\subset R$ and $A=T^{-1}R$, exterior-power and tensor localization identify $A\otimes_R\theta_s$ with the same construction for $i_A,p_A$; this equality is compatible with successive localizations. The assertions include $r=0$, $s_0=0$, characteristic two and the zero ring. When $r=0$ the map is the left unit identification followed by $\bigwedge^{s_0}(p^{-1})$, when $s_0=0$ it is the right unit identification followed by $\bigwedge^r i$, and when both vanish it is multiplication $R\otimes_R R\to R$.

source.place: Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), first proof, omitted verification of the local wedge isomorphism; the splitting, lift and basis invariance, localization and empty-wedge cases are made explicit.

proof.text: Apply the lifting characterization of projectivity to $\mathrm{id}_W$ and the surjection $p$ to obtain $s$ with $ps=\mathrm{id}_W$. Fix any such $s$. Since $p(v-s(pv))=0$, exactness and injectivity of $i$ give a unique $q_s(v)\in U$ with $i(q_s(v))=v-s(pv)$. Applying the injective map $i$ proves that $q_s$ is additive and $R$-linear. The identities $q_si=\mathrm{id}_U$, $q_ss=0$, $pi=0$, $ps=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $iq_s+sp=\mathrm{id}_V$ show directly that $(q_s,p)$ and $t_s$ are inverse linear maps. Only the lifting property already stated in the cited definition is used.

source.place: Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), first proof: detailed verification of the omitted local wedge construction.

proof.text: For any multiplicative subset $T$, localize each map by $h_T(m/a)=h(m)/a$. These maps preserve sums and scalar multiplication, composition and identities by their fraction formulas. Also $(U\oplus W)_T\cong U_T\oplus W_T$: send $(u,w)/a$ to $(u/a,w/a)$, with inverse $(u/a,w/b)\mapsto(bu,aw)/(ab)$. Thus all five identities of step 1 hold over $A=T^{-1}R$, and $t_{s_T}$ has inverse $(q_{s,T},p_T)$. In particular $i_T$ is injective, $p_T$ is surjective, and if $p_T(v)=0$ then $v=i_Tq_{s,T}(v)$; hence the localized sequence is split exact. This proves the localization assertions even before any freeness assumptions.

The exterior map of a linear map $h:M\to N$ is obtained by sending each tensor $m_1\otimes\cdots\otimes m_n$ to $h(m_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes h(m_n)$ and descending to the quotient: each defining relation $x\otimes x$ maps to $h(x)\otimes h(x)$. It sends a pure wedge to the wedge of the images. On these spanning wedges its composites and identity agree with the corresponding exterior maps. Apply this to the inverse maps $t_s$ and $(q_s,p)$ from step 1: $\bigwedge^n t_s$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\bigwedge^n(q_s,p)$, including $n=0$, where both maps are the identity on $R$.

Now assume the stated finite bases of $U,W$ of lengths $r,s_0$. Apply the direct-sum top-exterior theorem to $U,W$: its concatenation map is $c_{U,W}$ (inverting the displayed isomorphism there if necessary to use the concatenation direction). Composing it with the isomorphism $\bigwedge^{r+s_0}t_s$ from step 3 gives $\theta_s$. On a tensor of arbitrary pure wedges this composite is $i(u_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge i(u_r)\wedge s(w_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge s(w_{s_0})$, since $t_s(u,0)=i(u)$ and $t_s(0,w)=s(w)$. The cited theorem supplies an isomorphism for every pair of finite bases, without any assumption that the ring is a field.

source.place: Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), first proof: detailed verification of the omitted local wedge construction.

proof.text: For arbitrary lifts, exactness gives $v_k=s(w_k)+i(a_k)$ for some $a_k\in U$. Expand their wedge by multilinearity. The term with no $i(a_k)$ is the formula in step 4. Every other term has all $r$ vectors $i(u_j)$ and at least one further vector $i(a_k)$. Move one such vector next to the first block using $x\wedge y=-y\wedge x$. That block is the image of $u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_r\wedge a_k\in\bigwedge^{r+1}U$, which is zero by the exterior-basis theorem, as $r+1>r$. Its product with the remaining factors is zero. Thus every error term vanishes, proving exactly the asserted arbitrary-lift formula. This also works for $r=0$: then $U=0$ and $\bigwedge^1U=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), first proof: detailed verification of the omitted local wedge construction.

proof.text: Pure wedges span each exterior power, and pure tensors span their tensor product. Consequently the formula of step 5 determines the whole linear map uniquely. For a second section $s\prime$, use $s\prime(w_k)$ as the lift tuple in that formula: the maps $\theta_s$ and $\theta_{s\prime}$ agree on every spanning tensor of pure wedges, hence are equal. The concatenation construction $c_{U,W}$ is characterized without a chosen basis, and step 5 holds for arbitrary tuples. Therefore changing either basis leaves the map unchanged and the same formula holds for all replacement bases. No determinant or change-of-basis identity is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), first proof: detailed verification of the omitted local wedge construction.

proof.text: Write $M_T=T^{-1}M$. The identification $A\otimes_R M\cong M_T$ sends $(a/t)\otimes m$ to $am/t$, with inverse $m/t\mapsto(1/t)\otimes m$. It is well defined: $u(t\prime m-tm\prime)=0$ implies $(1/t)\otimes m-(1/t\prime)\otimes m\prime=(1/(utt\prime))\otimes u(t\prime m-tm\prime)=0$; the inverse identities and additivity follow by the tensor relations. In particular localization of a finite basis is a basis, by localizing its coordinate isomorphism $M\cong R^n$ and using the coordinate fraction maps. The quotient construction of step 3, now with coefficients $R\to A$, gives $g_n:\bigwedge_R^nM\to\bigwedge_A^nM_T$ sending wedges to wedges of $m/1$. The cited exterior-localization theorem applies to this very map, since $M\to M_T$ is a localization; hence $\bigwedge_A^nM_T$ is the localization of $\bigwedge_R^nM$. The tensor-localization theorem applied to the two exterior modules gives the comparison for their tensor product, with formula $(x/a)\otimes(y/b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)/(ab)$. These are the exterior and tensor identifications used in the assertion.

To compare the two maps over $A$, it suffices by $A$-linearity to evaluate on $1\otimes((u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge u_r)\otimes(w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_{s_0}))$: these generate, since $m/t=(1/t)(m/1)$ and pure wedges and tensors span. Under the comparisons of step 7, both maps send this element to $i_T(u_1/1)\wedge\cdots\wedge i_T(u_r/1)\wedge s_T(w_1/1)\wedge\cdots\wedge s_T(w_{s_0}/1)$, by the pure-wedge formula already proved. Step 2 and the localized bases in step 7 verify all hypotheses of the localized construction. Equality on these generators proves the claimed equality with $A\otimes_R\theta_s$. For a further localization $A\to B$, the direct comparison and the iterated comparison both send $b\otimes(a\otimes m)$ to $ba\otimes m$ and send each wedge of original vectors to the wedge of their final images; they agree on the same spanning generators. Thus the equality respects the scalar-extension associativity identifications and is compatible with every successive localization.

An empty basis forces its module to be zero by the basis expansion, and the exterior-basis theorem identifies degree zero with $R$ via the empty wedge $1$. If $r=0$, $p$ is an isomorphism and its unique section is $p^{-1}$; the concatenation formula becomes $a\otimes\omega\mapsto a(\bigwedge^{s_0}p^{-1})(\omega)$, the asserted left unit map. If $s_0=0$, $i$ is an isomorphism and the formula is $\omega\otimes a\mapsto a(\bigwedge^r i)(\omega)$, the right unit map. If both vanish it is $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. Every use of alternation above is the relation $x\wedge x=0$, never division by $2$; hence characteristic two is included. If $R$ is the zero ring, or $0\in T$, all relevant unital modules over the corresponding zero ring are zero and all maps and inverse identities still hold.
